advisories.summary: Several config keys fail startup. An existing patricia database is kept and does not resync; a new database uses the flat backend.
advisories.action: Before restart: set Db.FlushOnExit to None, WalOnly, or Full (true/false is rejected; the default is now WalOnly); replace Blocks.PreWarmStateOnBlockProcessing with Blocks.PreWarming; change negative numbers, including Receipt.TxLookupLimit -1, to an unsigned value (the old -1 sentinel is 18446744073709551615); set FlatDb.HistoryRetention whenever you set a history window. Receipt.MaxBlockDepth now defaults to 1000.

advisories.summary: Archive configs enable flat history, but an existing patricia archive keeps working. Flat history does not backfill. New or resyncing mainnet nodes keep ancient history only from block 24600000.
advisories.action: To move an archive to the flat backend, resync or set FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true. Do not pass FlatDb.Enabled=false on a database that is already flat.

advisories.summary: FlatDb.Enabled=false is refused on an existing flat database. Removed config keys are reported as invalid. poacore configs that synced on 2.0.0 can refuse to start.
advisories.action: Remove FlatDb.EnablePreimageRecording, Db.PreimageDbRocksDbOptions, Db.PreimageDbAdditionalRocksDbOptions, LogIndex.VerifyRpcResponse, Grpc.Enabled, Grpc.Host, and Grpc.Port. On an existing flat database pass FlatDb.Enabled=true, or delete the flat, flatHistory, and persistedSnapshot directories and resync. A fresh flat node with FastSync and SnapSync disabled is refused.

advisories.summary: Sepolia Glamsterdam is epoch 353024. With Network.LocalIp unset, Linux and Windows listen on IPv6 as well as IPv4. Merge.CompactMemory now defaults to No. Receipt.MaxBlockDepth is 10000 again. A RocksDB repair of a flat database resyncs state unless FlatDb.OnRepair=Ignore.
advisories.action: Run a consensus client that supports Sepolia Glamsterdam before Oct 6, 2026, 13:53:36 UTC. Set Network.LocalIp=0.0.0.0 to stay IPv4-only. Archive nodes that cannot snap-resync should set FlatDb.OnRepair=Ignore.
